headline: Chinese short-video apps are flooded with AI-made wealthy-family dramas in which fungus, fingernails and chopsticks fight over an inheritance.
score_reason: Pool score kept: shows how cheap AI video feeds viral formulas, with platform numbers, but it is trend commentary.
importance_line: What changed: AI has made scripts and clips so cheap that near-identical absurd dramas now crowd Chinese video apps, which affects their viewers and creators; the view that the trend will fade is the author's opinion, not a finding.
summary: TopKlout, in an article republished by 36Kr, reports that AI-generated inheritance dramas, built on one fill-in-the-blank template in which everyday objects stand in for rich families, have spread across Douyin, Xiaohongshu and Kuaishou. It cites Douyin data showing 221,900 new AI short dramas from January to June 2026, 1,055 of them above 100 million views, and argues the template is a passing phase because it lacks memorable stories.
notes: Read at 36Kr, which carries the TopKlout article; source credited to TopKlout, the original author.
